subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor this product-wide localization contract now, and if so, is the proposed five-PR v1 boundary the scope owners want to standardize?
rationale: The RFC intentionally spans Gateway wire contracts, recipient state, CLI and UI behavior, plugin metadata, safety text, and release policy; source inspection cannot determine whether those teams want one shared contract or a narrower first phase.

options.title: Sponsor the staged RFC
options.body: Keep the PR in draft, complete the required maintainer discussion, resolve each named owner decision, add prototype proof, and then accept the five-stage plan.

options.title: Narrow the first RFC
options.body: Limit v1 to locale identity, resolution, and structured core messages while deferring plugin metadata, recipient storage, and release-blocking coverage gates.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Close or archive the draft if current localization ownership or maintenance capacity cannot support a product-wide contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged RFC
recommendation.body: Keep the PR in draft, complete the required maintainer discussion, resolve each named owner decision, add prototype proof, and then accept the five-stage plan.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior localization umbrella records the clearest product-direction statement from this person, making them the best available routing candidate for renewed sponsorship.
